# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.


Repository files:
flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

The user wants me to fix a bug in the flag parsing logic.
The bug is that a flag like "off " (with a trailing space) is being parsed as true.
I need to modify the `flags/parse.py` file to correct this behavior.

First, I will read the `flags/parse.py` file to understand the current parsing logic.
Then, I will identify the part of the code responsible for handling flag values and modify it to trim whitespace before parsing.
Finally, I will submit the changes.

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.
  11|     Raises ValueError if the text is empty or only whitespace.
  12|     """
  13|     word = text.lower()
  14|     if not word:
  15|         raise ValueError("empty flag")
  16|     return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
  17| 
  18| 
  19| def parse_flags(text):
  20|     """Parse a comma-separated list of switch words into a list of bools.
  21| 
  22|     Each item is interpreted with `parse_flag`. Items that are empty or only
  23|     whitespace are skipped, so "" gives [] and "on,,off" gives [True, False].
  24|     """
  25|     return [parse_flag(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]

The `parse_flag` function on line 6 is responsible for parsing individual flag words.
Line 13 `word = text.lower()` converts the input to lowercase.
Line 16 `return word not in _FALSE_WORDS` checks if the word is in the set of false words.

The issue is that whitespace is not being stripped before the check.
I need to add `text.strip()` before `text.lower()`.

I will modify line 13 to `word = text.strip().lower()`.

I have modified the `flags/parse.py` file to strip whitespace from the input before converting it to lowercase and checking against the false words. This should fix the issue where "off " was being treated as true.

Now I will submit the changes.

arguments.summary: Fixed flag parsing to correctly handle trailing whitespace. The `parse_flag` function now strips whitespace from the input before processing, ensuring that values like "off " are correctly interpreted as false.
